understand.concept: TreeSet stores unique elements in sorted order. LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order. A comparator that returns zero treats values as duplicates in a TreeSet.

explain.narrative:
## TreeSet and LinkedHashSet

TreeSet stores unique elements in sorted order. LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order. A comparator that returns zero treats values as duplicates in a TreeSet.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Set<Integer> values = new java.util.TreeSet<>(java.util.List.of(3,1,2)); System.out.println(values); } }
examples.explanation: TreeSet keeps unique values in sorted order.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Set<String> values = new java.util.LinkedHashSet<>(); values.add("B"); values.add("A"); values.add("B"); System.out.println(values); } }
examples.explanation: LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order and rejects duplicates.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Set<Integer> values = new java.util.TreeSet<>(); values.add(5); values.add(5); System.out.println(values.size()); } }
examples.explanation: TreeSet uniqueness follows its ordering comparison.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { java.util.Set<String> values = new java.util.TreeSet<>(java.util.Comparator.reverseOrder()); values.add("A"); values.add("C"); values.add("B"); System.out.println(values); } }
examples.explanation: A reverse Comparator changes sorted order.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println(new java.util.TreeSet<>(java.util.List.of("pear","apple","orange"))); } }
